svg.text: Measured 2026-09-14 from the devices themselves: RouterOS API (ports, bridges, bonds, MAC tables, leases), PVE API (guest NICs), and cluster/kube API. Facts only — the proposed VLAN carve is a separate diagram.
PANEL A — physical and L2, as it is today
· the PPPoE client rides the bridge, so the WAN
port sits inside the LAN's broadcast domain:
the bridge floods PPPoE discovery to every port
(ISP MACs learned on ether5 in the MAC table)
· measured: 20 MB download → ether5 rx +24.8 MiB
(from the ISP), ether4 tx +24.6 MiB (to the LAN)
· `vpn` WireGuard interface exists with NO peers
· 10 dst-nat port-forwards on the WAN today
(1 member live — the other NIC left
the bond to become the 10G NAS link)
Everything in this panel is ONE flat L2 domain at 172.16.100.0/24: no VLAN exists anywhere, and every port defaults into it — which is why an unmapped port breaks silently rather than loudly.
PANEL B — networks, and where the data actually lives
carries: cluster, NAS LAN side, work PC,
AP + TV + gaming PC, IPMIs, IoT
Julia: not reachable from the LAN by design
NAS at .0.250 (its 10G path to the Sparks)
separate bridge — the carve must not touch it
sustained by design, not by luck
balteus vmbr3 — its LAN path is vmbr0,
a different bridge; this one has no
physical member: a fast VM↔VM path
that never hits a wire. Excluded from
the sweep — its absence is not a gap
PPPoE over the ISP's bridged Huawei
no CGNAT ⇒ inbound WireGuard is possible
(orphan — its key leaked and it should go)
the port carries NO link — unused
kept as a cleanup candidate, not a segment
greenfield: no migration cost when VPN lands
MinIO runs as a TrueNAS app on the NAS
no DNS, no ingress, no cluster in that path
⇒ readable even if the cluster is down
devops cluster (this LAN): main-* on balteus,
the ARC CI runner lives in the OTHER one
· every box is measured, not remembered
· panel A is one broadcast domain today
· panel B is L3: what connects to what
· the two islands are isolation, not trust
Not shown: the 4× LACP-bonded guests on the storage island (listed in the wiring doc), the 46-guest inventory, and the egress classes — those belong to the proposed plan, not to the as-is map.
Open, tracked elsewhere: Wi-Fi is one untrusted segment by decision; the WAN sits inside the LAN bridge until the pre-carve change; atuin's ports are reserved; bukefalos' bond idles.
Sources: RouterOS /interface, /interface/bridge/{port,vlan,host}, bond + PPPoE reads · PVE guest net* configs · cluster API · DHCP leases
portfolio: devops-cluster · terraform/docs/agent/network-wiring.md carries the detail
